rationale: Final small source step near expiry: checking whether anything contains the panic paths found earlier, so the malformed-input lead is recorded with its actual consequence. Reading only; no finding is confirmed and no obligation is created.

feedback.answered: Nothing in the library recovers a panic and the dispatch path has no containment. A search for recover() across the non-test sources finds no call, and processRPC dispatches directly to appendEntries (raft.go 1390-1413) on the main thread, so any panic raised while handling an RPC or while applying an entry leaves the goroutine and terminates the process. Two malformed-entry panic paths are now sourced and both are reachable from a single peer message that carries an entry the library does not validate: a LogConfiguration entry whose Data is not a valid msgpack Configuration panics inside DecodeConfiguration (configuration.go 356-372) when processConfigurationLogEntry decodes it during append (raft.go 1585-1596), and an entry with an unrecognized log Type panics in prepareLog's default branch (raft.go 1362-1389) when the entry is applied through processLogs. Entry Type and Data are stored by appendEntries without validation, so neither requires accumulated state or a sequence of messages, only one entry delivered by a sender that is not crash-stop-correct, or corruption on the wire or disk.
remaining: This remains a reading lead, not a confirmed finding: it needs a non-crash-stop sender or corrupt durable/wire data, which the crash-stop fault model the library is written against does not admit.

Whether the panics are deliberate policy for states the authors consider impossible is not established from the sources; both panic sites carry explanatory messages suggesting intent, which is why no obligation is claimed.
No execution witnesses a malformed entry reaching either panic, and with the remaining budget no further check was constructed.
